heading: INT. CUCKOO CLOCK REPAIR SHOP - EVENING

units.text: INT. CUCKOO CLOCK REPAIR SHOP - EVENING
A narrow shop in a Bavarian alley.
Hundreds of carved clocks ticking out of sync.
Pendulums swing like drunken metronomes.
A brass lamp hangs over a workbench strewn with tiny gears.
HORATIO PIMM (60s, a retired detective in a moth-eaten waistcoat, magnifier on his forehead) bends over a gutted clock, humming.
MISS LAVINIA GRAY (50s, gray bun, gloves buttoned to the wrist) sits primly in the customer's chair.
DR. EUSTACE KROLL (40s, doctor's bag, thick glasses, nervous smile) paces behind her.
It's a charming movement, Miss Gray. Eighteen-forty, I'd say.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: It was my husband's.
units.name: LAVINIA

units.text: Ah. Then it has seen some history.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Miss Gray, we really should be getting on.
units.name: EUSTACE

units.text: Doctor, I'm in no hurry.
units.name: LAVINIA

units.text: He stops.
Checks his watch.
Puts it away.
Tell me, Miss Gray. Your husband. When did he die?
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Last Thursday.
units.name: LAVINIA

units.text: And you've come to repair his clock so soon.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: He asked me to.
units.name: LAVINIA

units.text: Did he?
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Horatio lifts a tiny brass cog from the clock.
Turns it in the lamplight.
This isn't a clock part. It's a lock. A pharmacy lock.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Eustace goes pale.
Lavinia does not move.
The ticking seems to grow louder.
Inspector, I can explain.
units.name: EUSTACE

units.text: I'm retired. But go on.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: Eustace lunges for the door.
Lavinia whips a hatpin from her sleeve.
Horatio ducks under the workbench.
The doctor trips on the rug and slams into a grandfather clock.
All the clocks begin to chime at once.
Cuckoos burst out of every window.
In the din, Horatio rises, hatpin quivering in the wood a hand's width from his ear.
Lavinia and Eustace face each other, panting.
Both look at the clocks.
Both look at him.
Eight o'clock. Right on time.
units.name: HORATIO

units.text: You fool. He was dying anyway.
units.name: LAVINIA

units.text: Yes. But not on Thursday.
units.name: HORATIO
